speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness; to help me determine the cause, have you noticed if these symptoms worsen with activity or improve with rest?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The symptoms of diplopia on vertical gaze, proximal weakness worsening with activity and improving with rest, and the absence of sensory deficits are classic for this condition. I recommend requesting antibody testing and a Chest X-Ray to check for thymoma or thymic hyperplasia. REQUEST TEST: Anti-AChR Antibodies, Anti-MuSK Antibodies; REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray.
